text.p: Shares in British building society-turned-bank Alliance & Leicester Plc began trading on Monday at 542.5 pence per share before moving to around 545.0 p/shr when the company was floated on the London stock exchange.

At this higher price 2.2 million new shareholders -- the savers and borrowers who each received 250 free shares as a result of voting to ditch the Alliance's mutual tradition in favour of becoming a quoted company -- would each get a windfall of around 1,360 pounds ($2,220).

Institutional investors had already had a chance to show their interest in the new stock following an auction last Friday by stockbrokers Cazenove of free shares offered by individual shareholders who decided to cash in their windfall immediately. This resulted in an average price of 522 pence per share.

A total of 157 million shares, or 27 percent of the company, is being made available via a series of three auctions. More than 52 million were sold at the first auction, the second is due to take place later and the third on Tuesday. Abbey National, the first building society to become a bank, saw its shares rise 13.0 pence to 811.5 pence at 0738 GMT.
Alliance & Leicester's opening price has been boosted by takeover talk, with market rumours on Friday suggesting several institutions were bidding aggressively for shares at the first auction.

The company is the first building society, traditionally Britain's main home loan organisations, to be floated during 1997 but others, notably Halifax, Woolwich and Northern Rock are due to follow suit, with the promise of multi-billion pound windfalls for their members. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
